findings.label: Year-End Spending Pattern
findings.detail: Housing spent 5.1x their monthly average in March (£2.6M above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
findings.context_note: March spending above the monthly average is expected for UK councils on April–March fiscal years. Compare against prior years' March figures for meaningful analysis.

findings.label: Benford's Law Anomaly
findings.detail: Significant deviation from Benford's Law (p < 0.001). Digit 5 deviates 6.9% from expected distribution across 7,780 transactions. Note: with 7,780 transactions, chi-squared tests are highly sensitive — the 6.9% max digit deviation is the more practical measure of anomaly.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 7,780+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (6.9%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 7,913 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 0 deviates 4.55% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=7,913.
